correctness.rationale: Minimal-nonface components give the unique join factorization: no minimal nonface crosses exactly those partitions which exhibit a join. Thus reduced numerator and denominator record the positive and negative prime exponents, and continuity in the downset Alexandrov topology is signed-coordinate monotonicity. A column-finite homomorphism matrix may have infinite rows a priori. In any row with two nonzero entries, choose a one-coordinate input with output magnitude larger than the absolute coefficient of the second input. Appending a new unit coordinate with either sign is an upward move; choose the sign that decreases the output magnitude. An offset in a nonconstant row also fails, by comparing zero to a one-coordinate input with sufficiently large coefficient of the opposing sign. Constants and single unshifted scalar multiples preserve the order, including negative multipliers. Column finiteness and finite offset support suffice even at infinite rank. In a bijective map surjectivity excludes constant rows, repeated use of an input, and nonunit coefficients; injectivity excludes unused inputs. The nonnegative prime-image matrix of a unital join map gives precisely pairwise disjoint image supports; ordinary join divisibility is always preserved. The displayed injection is witnessed by (0,-1) below (1,-1), whose images fail the relation in the second coordinate.

value.rationale: Continuity is not automatic in this natural group completion. An intrinsic exact test on the images of prime generators identifies which algebraic morphisms survive continuously, including the failure of an injective monoid substitution whose group extension is an algebraic automorphism. This gives a reusable structural classification, not just a discontinuity counterexample or a rephrasing of order preservation.
residual_risks: Only affine maps and this specific topology are addressed; no added novelty or value is assigned to general homeomorphism rigidity.
